claims.text: An active-learning-trained machine-learned interatomic potential can reliably reproduce ab initio free energies in both solid and liquid phases.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can approach the accuracy of their underlying DFT calculations for elemental and multicomponent systems.
A moment tensor potential for bcc MoNbTaW provides a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost and yields test-set energy errors near 4.3 meV per atom.
The proposed potential can reproduce vibrational entropy in both solid and liquid phases.
The proposed potential can reproduce anharmonic free-energy contributions in both solid and liquid phases.
The proposed potential can reproduce electron–vibration coupling contributions.
Elemental or binary systems transform into multicomponent high-entropy alloys or liquids under the stated fusion conditions.
A limited set of DFT or ab initio molecular-dynamics calculations is sufficient to calibrate the proposed potential for phase free-energy calculations.
The trained potential can rapidly evaluate free energies over the full temperature ranges of both solid and fluid states.
The method is applicable from near room temperature to well above melting.
A potential encoding local structural features and bonding interactions thereby retains the relevant vibrational and anharmonic effects.
Encoding local structural features and bonding interactions retains aspects of electron–vibration coupling.
Active learning can identify the key regions of phase space needed for accurate solid and liquid free energies.
Training on a judiciously selected subset of ab initio molecular-dynamics data greatly reduces the number of expensive ab initio simulations required.
The surrogate model mitigates the cost escalation of TOR-TILD specifically for multicomponent systems.
The method will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude relative to TOR-TILD.
Predicted solid and liquid free energies will remain within approximately 5% of explicit ab initio results.
The method is expected to remain applicable to high-entropy alloys containing up to five or six principal elements.
Applicability may fail for extremely complex compositions or when nonlinear electron–vibration interactions dominate.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis confidently says the potential can reliably reproduce free energies including electron–vibration coupling, and the mediator says it retains that coupling, while the uncertainty field explicitly questions whether the surrogate can fully capture this contribution.
